summary: A box that a change merely ADDED can now be marked with the accent and named once in the legend, instead of buying a callout to say so. It applies where colour is free to carry it: the architecture figure, whose role colours say what a box is, and the ER, where every table is a store. It does NOT apply to the class figure, whose four role colours stand in for a distinction of the author's — a fifth colour meaning would compete with four the reader still has to be told, so that one keeps its callout and gains the legend it was missing. So two of the reference corpus's seven notes are gone. Read the counts, not the seconds: the engine did not get faster at placing a callout, the corpus stopped asking it to place two of them, and a real document gets the same saving for the same reason.
why: A box marked new may be explained by a legend entry rather than a note. The validator accepts either, refuses both being absent so the accent can never ship unexplained, and refuses the accent outright on a drawing whose legend already explains a role colour. A class diagram painting its types more than one colour with no legend is now advised on, since role names on a set of types never explain themselves.
